justifications.functional_suitability: Cataloguing of physical and digital items (R-01) is fully supported by Catalog & Search Service, Content Provider Integration Client, and Circulation Service, alongside comprehensive self-service and management capabilities across Patron SPA Component and Staff SPA Component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Requirement R-05 (<800ms search) is addressed directly via a dedicated Elasticsearch container, internal gRPC transport between API Gateway and Catalog & Search Service, and asynchronous inventory projections decoupled through Internal Event Bus.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is well designed with explicit integrations to external Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby), Identity Provider (OAuth2/OIDC), Payment Gateway, and EU-hosted Log & Metrics Aggregator using standard REST, OTLP, and gRPC protocols.
justifications.usability: The design serves Library Patrons, Librarians, and Administrators through Patron Web App & Staff Portal, dividing responsibilities into Patron SPA Component and Staff SPA Component, though administrative tooling details remain grouped within staff views.
justifications.reliability: Reliability is well planned using Resilience & Tracing Filter (Resilience4j circuit breaking), Dead Letter Queue Topics in Kafka, Dispatch & Retry Manager, and Velero for cluster state backup and recovery.
justifications.security: EU data residency constraints are enforced across EU-central infrastructure, EU-hosted databases, and EU third parties. Postgres RLS, pgaudit, pg_partman for GDPR data purging, and OAuth2/JWT validation in Security & Rate Limiting Filter provide robust protection.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture exhibits high modularity with independent microservices (Catalog & Search Service, Circulation Service), decoupled asynchronous messaging via Internal Event Bus, and strict contract enforcement using Confluent Schema Registry.
justifications.portability: Portability is assured through standardized containerization on Managed Kubernetes Cluster (agnostic between EKS/AKS) managed declaratively with GitOps Operator (ArgoCD).

PERF-01.justification: Reactive Spring Cloud Gateway, internal gRPC, and dedicated Elasticsearch indexing on NVMe storage with Kubernetes autoscaling easily sustain high concurrent throughput within 800 ms.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch shard sizing and JVM memory allocation
tradeoffs: Elasticsearch resource overhead vs. sub-second query performance

PERF-02.justification: Catalogue updates are decoupled via the Internal Event Bus (Kafka) and indexed asynchronously by the Event Consumer, preventing index mutation locks from degrading concurrent search queries.
sensitivity_points: Kafka consumer lag and Elasticsearch index refresh interval
tradeoffs: Near real-time search eventual consistency vs. search throughput under peak load

AVAIL-01.justification: Elasticsearch distributed clustering handles node failures transparently, while circulation operates on a completely independent PostgreSQL database, ensuring zero interruption or transaction loss.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cluster replica factor and failover election time
tradeoffs: Index replica storage overhead vs. cluster fault tolerance

AVAIL-02.justification: Patron SPAs are stateless, and traffic is managed by the Ingress Controller and API Gateway with Resilience4j circuit breakers, seamlessly rerouting traffic across redundant instances.
sensitivity_points: Health check interval and gateway circuit breaker thresholds
tradeoffs: Aggressive health check polling vs. network and gateway overhead

MOD-01.justification: The Content Provider Integration Client encapsulates external digital provider communication; however, lack of a dynamic plugin architecture may require modifying and rebuilding the Catalog & Search Service.
sensitivity_points: Loose coupling and generic abstractions within the integration client
tradeoffs: Co-locating integration clients in service vs. dedicated integration adapters

MOD-02.justification: The PolicyOverrideComponent handles policy evaluation, but no externalized rule engine, policy repository, or runtime configuration mechanism is specified to guarantee runtime changes without code redeployment.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic policy evaluation and configuration refresh mechanisms
tradeoffs: Complex runtime rule-engine management vs. static hardcoded business policies

SEC-01.justification: EU data residency is enforced throughout: EKS/AKS in EU-central, EU-hosted PostgreSQL, EU-perimeter logging, and EU-specific external integrations (Auth0 EU, Stripe EU, Twilio EU).
sensitivity_points: Strict regional binding of all third-party managed SaaS integrations
tradeoffs: Restricting vendor availability to EU endpoints vs. global multi-region redundancy

SEC-02.justification: Security is enforced at multiple layers: Gateway JWT validation, tenant context extraction, PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS), and comprehensive audit logging with pgaudit and OpenTelemetry.
sensitivity_points: Correct propagation of patron claims and strict database RLS policy enforcement
tradeoffs: Row-level security evaluation overhead vs. robust multi-tenant authorization
